situation:
You are the promotions manager at GRANITE RIDGE SPEEDWAY GROUP, a motorsports speedway operator and the regional leader in its home state. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to recommend how concessions should be priced at the company's first out-of-state track, which opens its season in April, and to explain that recommendation to the fans it takes something away from.

The company has run its home track for more than twenty years, and in all of that time it has let fans carry in their own coolers. About two thousand season ticket holders, whose passes are good at both tracks, use that policy every race. Concessions spending averages nine dollars a fan, roughly half of what the lenders who financed the new track were shown when the expansion was approved.

One plan bundles food and drink into the ticket price at the new track. Every ticket would include a meal, the offer would be promoted by email and through push notifications in the company's app, and spending per fan would be counted at the gate rather than estimated afterward. The plan is fair to the families who buy food at the track anyway, and it charges the season ticket holders who bring coolers for food they will not eat.

The other plan keeps the cooler policy and pushes discounted concessions to fans through the app instead, tracked by the redemption code each notification carries. The season ticket holders keep what they have always had, the fans who do not use the app pay full price at the window for the same food, and the new track would open its season with spending per fan where it is now, short of what the lenders were shown.

The vice president of operations (judge) wants your recommendation on which plan the new track opens with, how it would be communicated to the fans who lose something under it, and how the company would know afterward what the promotion did. The vice president of operations (judge) will greet you in the office and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the vice president of operations (judge) will thank you for your work.
